festivals: Annual Jatra (Chaitra, March–April, coinciding with Ramanavami)

history.period: 1413 (stone inscription; temple stands where originally built)
history.summary: The temple dates to 1413 under Vijayanagara ruler Veer Pratap Devaraya, evidenced by a stone inscription recording that Purush Shennvi's son Maee Shennvi of Kullalogram (Cuncolim) granted the village of Bandode (Bandivade) for the rituals of Shri Nagesh and Shree Mahalakshmi. Stone idols of Shiva, Parvati and Ganesha are said to date to the 7th century. Unlike most Goan temples, it was never destroyed or relocated during Portuguese rule because it stood in the Antruj of Ponda Mahal, outside Portuguese control; it was later renovated under the Marathas (Chatrapati Shahu of Satara) and again extensively in 1880. The deity is a swayambhu (self-manifested) lingam, discovered per legend when a cowherd saw a cow showering milk on a stone in a Shami grove. The mandapa galleries carry wood carvings of Ramayana and Mahabharata scenes; the lake in front reflects the idol and deepstambha. Opening hours conflict across sources: TimesTravel reports 5:30 AM–11:00 PM, velpu reports 5:30 AM–8:30 PM (flagged as conflicting). CSV town corrected from 'Ponda' to 'Bandora' (temple is at Donshiwado, Bandora village, Ponda taluka).

name: Shri Nagesh Temple
town_description: Bandora is a village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, near Ponda town, famous for its cluster of ancient temples (Nagesh, Ramnath, Mahalakshmi). It won the Ministry of Tourism's 'Best Tourism Village 2024' in the spiritual and wellness category.
tradition: Hindu (Shaiva; kuladevata of Gauda Saraswat Brahmins, Smarta sect)

travel.railway: Karmali (nearest); Madgaon ~21.5 km; Vasco da Gama ~37 km
travel.road: Off the Farmagudi–Bandora road, Ponda taluka; ~26 km from Panaji

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the annual Chaitra Jatra (March–April) is the main festival
